rationale: Contemporary general and specialized systems provide relevant comparative evidence. However, the prediction concerns ease of reproduction at an unspecified level and bundles a separate claim about experience, so existing benchmarks resolve only proxies.

operationalization: Formalize a universal recognizer that decides whether arbitrary data have a description below a fixed simplicity bound, then reduce the halting problem or use uncomputability of Kolmogorov complexity to show that no such complete method exists. Constructive recognizers for restricted classes establish the stated qualification.
obstacles: The result requires formal definitions of description language and complete generality.
Finite data always admit trivial literal descriptions.
rationale: Established computability results directly settle the impossibility of a complete general recognizer under standard formalizations. They also permit higher methods to recognize additional restricted regularities without contradicting the theorem.
